messages.subject: Backwards selection for LGCP model
parts:
Hi, 

I am fitting a model with 5 covariates included in the "full model." I am trying to use backwards selection to get to the "best" model (assuming that this should be measured through DIC). The code I've got for the full model is as below:

cmpfull <- coordinates ~
  LRoad(Covariates$LRoad, model = "linear") +
  Forest(Covariates$Forest, model = "linear") +
  SRoad(Covariates$SRoad, model = "linear") +
  Village(Covariates$Village, model = "linear") +
  mySPDE(coordinates, model = matern) +
  lsig(1) +
  Intercept(1) 

hn <- function(distance, lsig) {1 - exp(-(distance / (exp(lsig)))^-1)}

form <- coordinates + distance ~ mySPDE +
  log(hn(distance, lsig)) +
  Intercept + log(2)

matern <- inla.spde2.pcmatern(mesh,
                              prior.sigma = c(1, 0.01),
                              prior.range = c(10, 0.9)) 

fitfull <- lgcp(
  components = cmpfull,
  data = nests,
  samplers = transects,
  domain = list(
    coordinates = mesh,
    distance = INLA::inla.mesh.1d(seq(0, W, length.out = 30))
  ),
  formula = form,
  options = list(bru_initial = list(lsig = 2),
                 bru_verbose=4)
)


What would be the correct way to use backwards selection to get to a model that only includes the most powerful covariates? Is there a way to do this without going through every iteration of the model to see which has the lowest DIC? Any help much appreciated!

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Backwards selection for LGCP model
parts:
Hi Lucy,

disregarding the wider question of whether these types of variable
selection methods should really be used at all, then no, there isn't
really a faster way than going through all the models that the
backwards selection method needs to compare.
You can/should help it by setting initial values though, so the
optimiser gets some help; As long as it's only the covariates, it's
easy; just supply values for the latent variable estimate for each
component in bru_initial.
Something like
bru_linitial=list(LRoad = other_model_result$summary.fixed["LRoad",
"mode"], ...)

Finn

It seems your data uses metres as units, but your max.edge value seems to be intended to be in km? It might be that it’s trying to create a very very dense mesh.

Make sure to install the very latest version of fmesher, and replace the inla.mesh.2d call with a call to the fmesher function fm_mesh_2d (same parameters) and let me know if that helps or not (after making sure max.edge is in the appropriate units).
When converting the INLA package version of fmesher to a standalone package, I fixed some potential infinite loops that could happen for some special input data, so the new function should be more robust.  We haven’t merged the branch of INLA that will use the new fmesher package yet (but expect to do so soon, once fmesher gets onto CRAN).  I’m currently doing the last bug fixes and documentation of fmesher, and will send it to CRAN in the coming days most likely.

Finn
